title: Loading controls and honest blots
objective: Explain the role of a loading control and the ethics of blot presentation.

steps.title: Did you load equal protein?
steps.body: A **[[loading control]]** — a housekeeping protein (e.g. GAPDH, actin) or total-protein stain — shows each lane got similar protein. Without it, a 'bigger band' might just mean you loaded more, not that expression rose.

steps.prompt: Your target band is stronger in the treated lane. The loading control is *also* stronger there, by about the same amount. What can you conclude?
options: You likely just loaded more in that lane, not a real rise
Expression has clearly and genuinely increased with treatment
The loading control is unreliable here, so trust the target
The target rose, since the loading control is a separate protein
steps.explanation: If the loading control tracks the target, the difference is loading, not biology. Normalize target to the loading control.

variants.setup: Target up, loading control up by the same amount in the treated lane.
options: No — this is really just a loading difference
Yes, expression has genuinely gone up here now
Can't tell without repeating it with a new antibody
variants.reveal: Both rising together points to unequal loading, not changed expression.

steps.scenario: A published figure splices two non-adjacent lanes together with no dividing line, to put 'control' next to 'treated'.
options: Undisclosed splicing can mislead; any lane edits must be marked
Fine, as long as both lanes came from the very same gel
Fine, as long as both lanes had the identical exposure
steps.explanation: Rearranging or splicing lanes without a clear divider misrepresents the raw data. Journals require splices to be marked.
steps.followUp: Rule: show full blots where possible, mark any splice, and keep uncropped originals.

variants.prompt: Splicing blot lanes together without marking it is…
options: Misleading — any splices have to be disclosed
Fine, if both lanes came from the same blot
Fine, if both lanes had the same exposure

steps.title: The through-line
steps.body: qPCR has reference genes; westerns have loading controls; imaging has matched settings (C9). Every quantitative method needs a yardstick and honest presentation — the C1 mindset, in each assay.
